summary: Steam is a heavier train pick-up-and-deliver game where players build track networks, then run trains to fulfill goods deliveries for income or victory points. It rewards careful route planning and timing of upgrades, with tense decisions about spending on infrastructure versus banking points.
praised: Good player interaction over shared track and goods
criticised: Can feel fiddly with cubes and cards
Some find the theme thin compared to the mechanics

interaction.kind: auctioning for turn order and racing/blocking for the same track links and delivery cubes
interaction.detail: Every round opens with a cash auction where your bid directly costs an opponent position and money, and the shared board has a finite number of track hexes and city links, so laying track to complete your route often denies the exact link someone else needed. Goods cubes are drawn onto a shared map and picked over competitively, making a large share of the game state fought over rather than private.
interaction.said: Age of Steam's descendants are routinely called 'brutal', 'mean', and 'cutthroat' — players talk about the turn-order auction as a game in itself, and about 'blocking' track to strangle a rival's route.

scoring.how_you_win: Deliver goods across your rail network, choosing each time whether to advance your victory point marker or your income marker; the game ends when the goods-cube supply runs dry, and whoever's VP marker (after loan penalties) is furthest ahead wins.
